column2:
deadly(adj./adv.)致命的、極度的、極其
dead(adj.)死的
death(n.)死亡
deadly disease 致命的疾病
deadly serious 極為認真的
Some mushrooms in the forest are deadly if eaten.
(森林裡有些蘑菇吃了會致命。)
He was deadly serious about quitting his job to travel the world.
(他是極為認真地想辭職去環遊世界。)

debris(n.)殘骸、碎片、瓦礫
(無詞性變化)
space debris 太空垃圾
clear the debris 清除瓦礫
Rescue workers searched through the debris for survivors after the earthquake.
(地震過後，救難人員在瓦礫堆中搜尋生還者。)
Space debris has become a serious threat to satellites.
(太空垃圾已成為人造衛星的嚴重威脅。)

debut(n.)首次登台、初次亮相、處女作
(無詞性變化)
make one's debut 首次登場
debut album 首張專輯
The young singer made her debut on a TV talent show.
(那位年輕歌手在電視選秀節目上首次亮相。)
Their debut album sold over a million copies in its first year.
(他們的首張專輯第一年就賣出超過一百萬張。)

decay(n./v.)腐爛、蛀蝕、衰敗
decayed(adj.)腐爛的、蛀壞的
tooth decay 蛀牙
urban decay 都市衰敗
Eating too much candy can lead to tooth decay.
(吃太多糖果可能導致蛀牙。)
The old wooden house slowly decayed after years of neglect.
(那棟老木屋經過多年無人照料後漸漸腐朽。)

deceive(v.)欺騙、蒙蔽
deception(n.)欺騙
deceit(n.)欺詐、欺騙
deceptive(adj.)騙人的、誤導的
deceive oneself 自欺欺人
be deceived by 被⋯欺騙
Don't be deceived by his friendly smile.
(別被他友善的笑容給騙了。)
She deceived her parents about where she was going that night.
(她那晚對父母謊報了自己要去的地方。)

decent(adj.)像樣的、體面的、正派的
decency(n.)體面、正派
decently(adv.)體面地、像樣地
decent job 像樣的工作
decent salary 還不錯的薪水
After graduation, he found a decent job in a tech company.
(畢業後，他在一家科技公司找到一份不錯的工作。)
He is a decent man who always treats others with respect.
(他是個正派的人，總是尊重他人。)

declaration(n.)宣言、聲明、申報
declare(v.)宣布、申報
Declaration of Independence 獨立宣言
customs declaration 海關申報
The Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776.
(《獨立宣言》在1776年簽署。)
Travelers must fill out a customs declaration form before landing.
(旅客在降落前必須填寫海關申報單。)

decline(n./v.)下降、衰退、婉拒
(無詞性變化)
decline an invitation 婉拒邀請
in decline 衰退中
The number of births in Taiwan has declined sharply in recent years.
(近年來臺灣的出生人數急劇下降。)
She politely declined the invitation to the party.
(她禮貌地婉拒了派對的邀請。)

dedicate(v.)奉獻、致力於、題獻
dedication(n.)奉獻、專注
dedicated(adj.)專注的、盡心盡力的
dedicate oneself to 致力於⋯
dedicate a book to 把書獻給⋯
The doctor dedicated his life to fighting cancer.
(這位醫生畢生致力於對抗癌症。)
The author dedicated her new novel to her late mother.
(作者將她的新小說獻給已故的母親。)

defendant(n.)被告
defend(v.)防衛、辯護
plaintiff(n.)原告
the defendant's lawyer 被告律師
find the defendant guilty 判被告有罪
The jury found the defendant not guilty.
(陪審團判定被告無罪。)
The defendant's lawyer asked for more time to prepare.
(被告的律師要求更多時間準備。)

deficit(n.)赤字、不足額
(無詞性變化)
budget deficit 預算赤字
trade deficit 貿易逆差
The government is trying to reduce the budget deficit.
(政府正努力減少預算赤字。)
The country has had a trade deficit for five years in a row.
(這個國家已連續五年出現貿易逆差。)

defy(v.)違抗、公然反抗、無法(解釋等)
defiance(n.)反抗、蔑視
defiant(adj.)反抗的、挑釁的
defy the law 違抗法律
defy description 難以形容
The teenager defied his parents and went to the concert anyway.
(那名青少年違抗父母，還是去了演唱會。)
The beauty of the sunrise defies description.
(日出之美難以言喻。)

delegate(n./v.)代表、委派、授權
delegation(n.)代表團、授權
delegate tasks 分派任務
a delegate to the conference 會議代表
A good leader knows how to delegate tasks to team members.
(好的領導者懂得把任務分派給團隊成員。)
Each school sent two delegates to the student conference.
(每所學校派兩名代表參加學生會議。)

delegation(n.)代表團、授權、委派
delegate(n./v.)代表、委派
trade delegation 貿易代表團
lead a delegation 率領代表團
A trade delegation from Japan visited Taipei last week.
(一個來自日本的貿易代表團上週訪問臺北。)
Effective delegation allows managers to focus on important decisions.
(有效的授權讓主管能專注於重要決策。)

deliberate(adj./v.)故意的、深思熟慮的、仔細考慮
deliberately(adv.)故意地
deliberation(n.)深思熟慮、審議
a deliberate attempt 蓄意的企圖
deliberate on 仔細考慮⋯
I'm sure it was a deliberate lie, not a mistake.
(我確定那是蓄意的謊言，不是失誤。)
The committee deliberated for hours before reaching a decision.
(委員會商議了好幾個小時才做出決定。)

democrat(n.)民主主義者、(Democrat)美國民主黨員
democracy(n.)民主
democratic(adj.)民主的
a true democrat 真正的民主主義者
Democrats and Republicans 民主黨與共和黨
As a true democrat, she believes every citizen's voice matters.
(身為真正的民主主義者，她相信每位公民的聲音都很重要。)
The Democrats won a majority in the election.
(民主黨在選舉中贏得多數席次。)

denial(n.)否認、拒絕、否定
deny(v.)否認、拒絕
in denial 拒絕承認(事實)
a flat denial 斷然否認
He is still in denial about his poor grades.
(他仍不肯接受自己成績很差的事實。)
The company issued a firm denial of the rumors.
(公司對謠言發出強烈否認。)

density(n.)密度、稠密
dense(adj.)密集的
densely(adv.)密集地
population density 人口密度
high density 高密度
Hong Kong has one of the highest population densities in the world.
(香港是世界上人口密度最高的地方之一。)
Water has a higher density than oil.
(水的密度比油高。)

depict(v.)描繪、描述
depiction(n.)描繪、描述
depict A as B 把A描繪成B
vividly depict 生動地描繪
The painting depicts a busy market in old Taipei.
(這幅畫描繪了舊時臺北熱鬧的市集。)
The movie depicts the hero as a lonely but brave man.
(電影把主角描繪成一個孤獨卻勇敢的人。)

deploy(v.)部署、調度、有效運用
deployment(n.)部署、調度
deploy troops 部署軍隊
deploy resources 調度資源
The government deployed soldiers to help with flood relief.
(政府調派士兵協助救災。)
The company plans to deploy the new software next month.
(公司計畫下個月部署這套新軟體。)

depress(v.)使沮喪、使蕭條、壓下
depression(n.)沮喪、憂鬱症、不景氣
depressed(adj.)沮喪的
depressing(adj.)令人沮喪的
depress prices 壓低價格
depress the button 按下按鈕
Rainy weather always depresses me.
(下雨天總是讓我心情低落。)
The bad news depressed the stock market for weeks.
(這個壞消息使股市低迷了好幾週。)

deputy(n.)副手、代理人、副⋯
(無詞性變化)
deputy mayor 副市長
deputy director 副主任、副處長
The deputy mayor attended the ceremony on behalf of the mayor.
(副市長代表市長出席了典禮。)
She was promoted to deputy director last year.
(她去年被升為副主任。)

derive(v.)得到、源自、衍生
derivation(n.)起源、衍生
derivative(n./adj.)衍生物、衍生的
derive from 源自⋯
derive pleasure from 從⋯得到樂趣
Many English words are derived from Latin.
(許多英文字源自拉丁文。)
She derives great pleasure from helping others.
(她從幫助他人中獲得極大的樂趣。)

descend(v.)下降、下來、遺傳、源自
descent(n.)下降、血統
descendant(n.)後代、子孫
descend from 是⋯的後代
descend the stairs 走下樓梯
The plane began to descend toward the airport.
(飛機開始朝機場下降。)
She is said to be descended from a famous scholar.
(據說她是一位著名學者的後代。)

descriptive(adj.)描述的、描寫的
describe(v.)描述
description(n.)描述
descriptive writing 描寫文
descriptive language 描述性語言
Our teacher asked us to write a descriptive essay about our hometown.
(老師要我們寫一篇描寫家鄉的文章。)
The author uses rich descriptive language to bring the scene to life.
(作者運用豐富的描寫語言讓場景栩栩如生。)

despair(n./v.)絕望、失望
desperate(adj.)絕望的、拚命的
in despair 絕望地
despair of 對⋯感到絕望
He gave up in despair after failing the exam three times.
(他考了三次都沒過後，絕望地放棄了。)
Never despair; things will get better.
(永遠不要絕望，事情會好轉的。)

destination(n.)目的地、終點
destine(v.)注定
tourist destination 觀光勝地
final destination 最終目的地
Kenting is a popular tourist destination in summer.
(墾丁是夏天熱門的觀光勝地。)
We finally reached our destination after a ten-hour drive.
(經過十小時的車程，我們終於抵達目的地。)

destiny(n.)命運、天命
destined(adj.)注定的
control one's destiny 掌握自己的命運
by destiny 命中注定
She believes that we can shape our own destiny.
(她相信我們可以塑造自己的命運。)
Meeting him was destiny, not chance.
(遇見他是命中注定，不是偶然。)

destructive(adj.)破壞性的、毀滅性的
destroy(v.)破壞
destruction(n.)破壞
destructive power 破壞力
destructive behavior 破壞性行為
The typhoon was the most destructive storm in ten years.
(這個颱風是十年來破壞力最強的暴風雨。)
Constant criticism can be destructive to a child's confidence.
(不斷的批評可能會摧毀孩子的自信。)

devotion(n.)奉獻、熱愛、忠誠
devote(v.)奉獻
devoted(adj.)忠誠的、全心全意的
devotion to 對⋯的熱愛、奉獻
religious devotion 虔誠
His devotion to his students made him a beloved teacher.
(他對學生的全心奉獻使他成為一位受愛戴的老師。)
The dog showed great devotion to its owner.
(這隻狗對主人非常忠誠。)

diagnose(v.)診斷
diagnosis(n.)診斷
diagnostic(adj.)診斷的
be diagnosed with 被診斷出患有⋯
diagnose a problem 找出問題所在
He was diagnosed with diabetes at the age of forty.
(他在四十歲時被診斷出罹患糖尿病。)
The mechanic quickly diagnosed the problem with my car.
(技師很快就找出我車子的問題。)

diagnosis(n.)診斷
diagnose(v.)診斷
diagnostic(adj.)診斷的
make a diagnosis 做出診斷
early diagnosis 早期診斷
Early diagnosis of cancer can save many lives.
(癌症的早期診斷可以拯救許多生命。)
The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the X-ray.
(醫生看過X光片後做出了診斷。)

dialect(n.)方言
dialectal(adj.)方言的
local dialect 當地方言
speak a dialect 說方言
My grandparents speak to each other in the Hakka dialect.
(我的祖父母彼此用客家話交談。)
Many local dialects are disappearing as young people move to cities.
(隨著年輕人移居城市，許多地方方言正在消失。)

diameter(n.)直徑
radius(n.)半徑
in diameter 直徑為⋯
the diameter of a circle 圓的直徑
The pizza is about thirty centimeters in diameter.
(這個披薩的直徑大約三十公分。)
To find the area, first measure the diameter of the circle.
(要算出面積，先量出圓的直徑。)

diaper(n.)尿布
(無詞性變化)
change a diaper 換尿布
disposable diaper 紙尿布
The young father learned how to change a diaper.
(這位年輕爸爸學會了怎麼換尿布。)
Disposable diapers create a large amount of waste every year.
(紙尿布每年製造大量的垃圾。)

digestion(n.)消化、消化力
digest(v.)消化
digestive(adj.)消化的
aid digestion 幫助消化
poor digestion 消化不良
Drinking warm water after meals can aid digestion.
(飯後喝溫水可以幫助消化。)
Stress can have a negative effect on your digestion.
(壓力可能對你的消化造成負面影響。)

dilemma(n.)兩難、困境
(無詞性變化)
in a dilemma 進退兩難
face a dilemma 面臨兩難
I'm in a dilemma about whether to study abroad or stay home.
(我在出國念書還是留在國內之間進退兩難。)
Doctors often face moral dilemmas in their work.
(醫生在工作中常面臨道德上的兩難。)

dimension(n.)尺寸、面向、維度、層面
dimensional(adj.)⋯維的、⋯度空間的
three dimensions 三度空間、三維
a new dimension 新的面向
Please measure the dimensions of the room before buying furniture.
(買家具前請先量好房間的尺寸。)
Social media has added a new dimension to how we communicate.
(社群媒體為我們的溝通方式增添了新的面向。)

diminish(v.)減少、降低、貶低
diminution(n.)減少
diminish in value 價值降低
diminishing returns 報酬遞減
The pain gradually diminished after I took the medicine.
(吃藥後疼痛漸漸減輕了。)
Nothing can diminish her achievements.
(什麼也無法抹煞她的成就。)

diplomatic(adj.)外交的、圓滑的、有手腕的
diplomat(n.)外交官
diplomacy(n.)外交
diplomatic relations 外交關係
diplomatic answer 圓滑的回答
The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1990.
(兩國在1990年建立外交關係。)
She gave a diplomatic answer to avoid hurting anyone's feelings.
(她給了一個圓滑的回答，以免傷害任何人的感受。)

directory(n.)名錄、電話簿、(電腦)目錄
(無詞性變化)
telephone directory 電話簿
file directory 檔案目錄
You can find the store's number in the telephone directory.
(你可以在電話簿裡找到這家店的號碼。)
Save the file in the main directory.
(把檔案存在主目錄裡。)

disapprove(v.)不贊成、反對
disapproval(n.)不贊成、反對
approve(v.)贊成
disapprove of 不贊成⋯
strongly disapprove 強烈反對
My parents disapprove of my staying up late to play games.
(我爸媽不贊成我熬夜打電動。)
The teacher shook her head to show she disapproved.
(老師搖搖頭表示不贊同。)

disclose(v.)揭露、透露、公開
disclosure(n.)揭露、透露
disclose information 透露資訊
refuse to disclose 拒絕透露
The company refused to disclose the details of the deal.
(公司拒絕透露這筆交易的細節。)
Never disclose your password to anyone online.
(絕對不要在網路上把密碼透露給任何人。)

disconnect(v.)切斷、斷開、使分離
disconnection(n.)斷開、分離
disconnected(adj.)斷開的、不連貫的
disconnect from 和⋯斷開
get disconnected 斷線(電話、網路)
We got disconnected in the middle of our video call.
(我們視訊通話到一半就斷線了。)
Sometimes it's good to disconnect from social media for a while.
(有時暫時遠離社群媒體是好事。)

discourse(n.)論述、交談、演講
(無詞性變化)
political discourse 政治論述
public discourse 公共論述
Social media has changed the nature of political discourse.
(社群媒體改變了政治論述的本質。)
The professor gave a long discourse on modern art.
(教授針對現代藝術發表了一場長篇演講。)

discriminate(v.)歧視、區別
discrimination(n.)歧視、辨別力
discriminatory(adj.)歧視的
discriminate against 歧視⋯
discriminate between 區分⋯
It is illegal to discriminate against people because of their age.
(因年齡而歧視他人是違法的。)
Young children cannot always discriminate between fact and fiction.
(幼童不一定能分辨事實與虛構。)

discrimination(n.)歧視、辨別力
discriminate(v.)歧視、區別
discriminatory(adj.)歧視的
racial discrimination 種族歧視
discrimination against 對⋯的歧視
The law protects workers from discrimination in the workplace.
(這項法律保護勞工免於在職場上受到歧視。)
Gender discrimination is still a problem in many countries.
(性別歧視在許多國家仍是個問題。)

disrupt(v.)擾亂、使中斷、顛覆
disruption(n.)中斷、混亂
disruptive(adj.)破壞性的、擾亂的
disrupt traffic 擾亂交通
disrupt a class 擾亂課堂秩序
The typhoon disrupted train services across the island.
(颱風使全島的火車服務中斷。)
His loud phone call disrupted the whole class.
(他大聲講電話擾亂了整個課堂。)

dissolve(v.)溶解、解散、消失
dissolution(n.)解散、溶解
dissolve in water 溶於水
dissolve a partnership 解除合夥關係
Stir the sugar until it completely dissolves in the tea.
(攪拌糖直到它完全溶在茶裡。)
The band dissolved after their lead singer left.
(主唱離開後，樂團就解散了。)

distinction(n.)區別、差異、卓越、殊榮
distinct(adj.)不同的、明顯的
distinctive(adj.)獨特的
make a distinction between 區分⋯
with distinction 以優異成績
It's important to make a distinction between facts and opinions.
(區分事實與意見是很重要的。)
She graduated from university with distinction.
(她以優異成績從大學畢業。)

distinctive(adj.)獨特的、有特色的
distinct(adj.)不同的
distinction(n.)區別、特點
distinctive feature 獨特的特徵
distinctive style 獨特的風格
The singer has a very distinctive voice.
(這位歌手有非常獨特的嗓音。)
Tainan is known for its distinctive local food.
(臺南以獨具特色的在地小吃聞名。)

distract(v.)使分心、轉移(注意力)
distraction(n.)令人分心的事物
distracted(adj.)分心的
distract someone from 使某人從⋯分心
easily distracted 容易分心
The noise outside distracted me from my homework.
(外面的噪音讓我無法專心寫作業。)
Smartphones can easily distract students in class.
(智慧型手機很容易讓學生上課分心。)

doctrine(n.)教義、學說、主義
doctrinal(adj.)教義的、學說的
religious doctrine 宗教教義
political doctrine 政治主張
The monks spent years studying Buddhist doctrine.
(僧侶們花了多年研讀佛教教義。)
The president announced a new foreign policy doctrine.
(總統宣布了一項新的外交政策主張。)

document(n./v.)文件、記錄、證明
documentary(n./adj.)紀錄片、文件的
documentation(n.)文件、證明資料
official document 正式文件
document the process 記錄過程
Please sign the document and return it by Friday.
(請在文件上簽名並在週五前交回。)
The scientist carefully documented every step of the experiment.
(那位科學家仔細記錄了實驗的每一個步驟。)

documentary(n./adj.)紀錄片、文件的、紀實的
document(n./v.)文件、記錄
documentary film 紀錄片
documentary evidence 書面證據
We watched a documentary about climate change in class.
(我們在課堂上看了一部關於氣候變遷的紀錄片。)
The lawyer presented documentary evidence to the court.
(律師向法院提出書面證據。)

domain(n.)領域、範圍、領土、網域
(無詞性變化)
public domain 公共領域
domain name 網域名稱
Artificial intelligence is no longer just the domain of scientists.
(人工智慧已不再只是科學家的領域。)
We need to register a domain name for our website.
